items.title: Treasury Futures Fall as Rising Stock Futures Damp Haven Demand

There’s no cash trading in the Asia session due to a public holiday in Japan.

“US equity futures have rallied in Asia time this morning and this improvement in sentiment seems to be the driver of US Treasury weakness,” said Andrew Ticehurst, a senior strategist at Nomura in Sydney.
The drop in Treasury futures underscore how bonds are once again moving in the opposite direction to equities as investors debate if stocks are primed for a rebound.
“The AI selloff has dragged sentiment across markets, and if it resumes, Treasuries will see demand again,” said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research.

items.title: No deal: COP31 talks fail over fossil fuel mention
points: The gavel came down on Cop31 in Antalya on Sunday without its cover decision being adopted, after negotiations ran two days past the scheduled Friday close and countries failed to bridge differences over fossil fuels, climate finance and equity.
The collapse of the proposed Antalya Pact is a major setback for the Turkish and Australian Cop31 presidencies, with nearly 200 countries unable to agree on a common political outcome.

The European Union, the United Kingdom and several developing countries, including vulnerable island nations, opposed the final draft, which did not explicitly mention fossil fuels or commit to a clear pathway for moving away from them.
It was the first time since Cop15 in Copenhagen in 2009 that a summit’s cover decision was not formally adopted, and the first such failure since the Paris Agreement was adopted in 2015.
The summit overran its scheduled end on Friday, November 20, by more than 44 hours, beating the record set by Cop25 in Madrid in 2019.

The rally has been driven largely by record monthly foreign inflows of ₹1.14 trillion into Indian equities through 20 November, as investors reassess their exposure to expensive artificial intelligence (AI) and technology stocks in developed markets.

"These inflows are largely tactical and reflect portfolio diversification rather than a structural shift in foreign investors' allocation towards India,'' said Madhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global Financial Services.

items.title: IEA: Extreme Weather Risks to International Oil and Natural Gas Shipping
points: Extreme weather can damage port infrastructure, interrupt operations, and restrict or close routes, forcing costly delays or diversions.
In the IEA’s Stated Policies Scenario, international oil and natural gas shipping activity rises by over 15% by 2035, with LNG growing faster than oil.
Virtually all ports with regular tanker activity in Japan, Korea and China are exposed to a tropical cyclone at least once in 500 years on average.
Tanker-handling ports experience an average downtime of 1.5 days per year due to disruption from extreme weather, with around 60% of assessed ports losing less than one day annually.

Research estimates current annual weather-related physical damage to tanker-handling ports at around USD 5 billion, with Europe and North America accounting for nearly half of this due to the number and value of assets exposed.
By 2050, annual damage could nearly double in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) scenario associated with around 3 °C warming by the end of the century.

items.title: Two Supply Lines, One Terminal: 12 Sanctioned Tankers at the Houthi-Controlled Ras Issa

What Happened Twelve Sanctioned Tankers, Eleven of Them Dark Across the seven-week window, Windward identified 12 sanctioned tankers at the Houthi-controlled Ras Issa terminal and the nearby Salif anchorage.
Five broadcast false positions while sitting off Ras Issa, ranging from 80 nautical miles away (mid-Red Sea) to 2,800 nautical miles away (between Sri Lanka and Malaysia).
One case illustrates the pattern end to end: On June 9, about 130,400 barrels of Russian diesel was loaded at Taman onto a Russian-flagged tanker sanctioned under Russia programs.

items.title: Vessel renewal incentive policy in China: Potential greenhouse gas reduction impact and opportunities for improvement
points: Maritime shipping plays a key role in China’s national freight sector, accounting for over 50% of transportation activity in 2024.

Decarbonization of this sector at a rate in line with the government’s goal to achieve carbon neutrality before 2060 will require the large-scale application of ships fueled by low- and zero-carbon fuels.

China introduced policies in 2024 to promote the scrapping and renewal of old ships, which offer shipowners tiered subsidies to renew older ships before their mandatory retirement dates, with greater support for new/clean energy vessels (NCEVs).
This paper estimates the potential impact of the retire-and-renew (RNR) policy on fleet renewal and greenhouse gas emissions in China’s coastal fleet.

Using the Vessel Economic Guidance and Assessment (VEGA) model and Polaris, a shipping emissions projection model, we estimated fleet renewal and greenhouse gas emissions from 2025 to 2050 under the existing RNR policy design and two alternative scenarios.

items.title: How India can turn shipbuilding potential into industrial scale
points: India’s shipbuilding and ship repair opportunity extends beyond creating additional yard capacity.
It requires a coordinated approach to vessel demand, production capability, financing, suppliers and skills.

The FICCI–EY knowledge report, “Optimising India’s shipbuilding and ship repair capacity: Roadmap for industrial scaleup,” examines how these elements can develop together to support a competitive maritime industrial ecosystem.
The report assesses India’s current position against global industry benchmarks and considers the pathways followed by established shipbuilding economies.
Grouping compatible requirements into phased programs could help align shipbuilding financing, supplier investment and workforce planning with expected workloads.
This would give shipbuilding in India a clearer basis for scaling production.
Strengthening the shipbuilding value chain India’s existing capabilities in hull fabrication, block assembly and outfitting provide a foundation for expansion.
International partnerships can contribute where they support genuine capability transfer, domestic engineering and supplier qualification rather than remaining limited to licensing or assembly.

items.title: Russian cargo ship struck by drones in Gulf of Finland
points: The United States announced sanctions against the Sparta II in early May 2022, just over two months after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
A Russian cargo ship has been struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland, Finnish and Russian authorities have said.
Finnish Defence Forces detected the attack in international waters on Saturday morning, west of Suursaari, according to the country’s defence ministry.
The United States announced sanctions against the Sparta II in early May 2022, just over two months after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The Gulf of Finland is a crucial maritime passage for Russia, connecting Saint Petersburg with the wider Baltic Sea.
Finland’s defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was also suspected of violating Finnish airspace on Saturday afternoon, off the coast of Loviisa.
“The suspected airspace violation may be related to rescue or monitoring operations involving a cargo ship that sustained damage in the Gulf of Finland.

items.title: Singapore fuel oil stocks increase 7% amid higher net imports
points: Singapore’s residual fuel oil stocks have averaged 7% higher so far in November than across October, Enterprise Singapore’s latest data shows.
Fuel oil imports have increased by 429,000 bbls, while exports have declined by 205,000 bbls.
The UAE (23%) has been the largest source of Singapore’s fuel oil imports this month, followed by Russia (16%) and Saudi Arabia (10%), according to cargo tracker Vortexa.
On the export side, China (39%) has received the largest share of Singapore’s fuel oil cargoes, followed by Indonesia, the UAE and US (10% each).
Meanwhile, Singapore’s middle distillate inventories have fallen by 5% so far this month to 8.73 million bbls.
VLSFO lead times have extended to 15-17 days from 13-15 days a week earlier.
HSFO lead times have shortened to 9-12 days from 12-16 days last week.
Source: By Tuhin Roy, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/

items.title: Vietnam’s shipbuilding industry seizes opportunities from green transformation
points: One of the outstanding projects undertaken by HD Hyundai Vietnam Shipbuilding Co. , Ltd. (HVS) is the construction of the LR2 oil tanker, a dual-fuel LNG vessel incorporating rigid sail technology (Wind Wings), with a deadweight tonnage of 115,000 DWT.
Starting with ship repair, HVS transitioned to complete new shipbuilding in 2008 and has grown into one of the world’s largest shipyards.
To date, HVS has delivered 210 vessels, including cargo ships with a tonnage of up to 87,000 tons and oil tankers up to 115,000 tons, to customers in many countries around the world.

As a joint venture between the Shipbuilding Industry Corporation (SBIC) and Hyundai Group ( Korea ), after nearly 30 years of operation, HVS is considered an effective and sustainable cooperation model, benefiting both parties.
New shipbuilding at HD Hyundai Vietnam Shipbuilding Co. , Ltd. Photo provided by HVS.

items.title: Spain to ban all scrubber wastewater discharge in its ports
points: Spain has banned ships from discharging wastewater from any type of scrubber in its ports and anchorages from 1 July 2027 to protect the marine environment, the transport ministry said.
Spain’s Council of Ministers approved the royal decree on Tuesday.

The ministry said the decree would establish a uniform framework in place of local restrictions already in force at several Spanish ports, including Algeciras, Almería, Barcelona, Cartagena, Huelva and Valencia.

Spain’s move complies with the OSPAR Commission’s decision agreed in June last year, under which 15 European governments and the EU agreed to stop ships from discharging scrubber washwater in ports and internal waters.
Each OSPAR member must ban discharges from open-loop scrubbers in internal waters and ports by 1 July 2027, and from scrubbers in any mode by 1 July 2029.
There are currently 7,230 ships equipped with scrubbers across the world, with the number expected to increase to 7,612 vessels by 2029, according to DNV data.

items.title: China: Imported iron ore losses narrow as market waits on APEC summit
points: The average imported iron ore margin rose from -14.83 yuan/mt to -13.08 yuan/mt, narrowing losses slightly.
The improvement was mainly supported by a small rise in spot prices.
Most market participants stayed on the sidelines during the APEC leaders’ summit, waiting for clearer policy signals.
Futures rose in the morning but lacked follow-through buying, and gains narrowed in the afternoon.
In the spot market, traders priced in line with the market and mills bought on an as-needed basis.
Iron ore prices are likely to stay range-bound in the short term.
The market will watch for policy statements during the summit and when mills start winter restocking.
The average imported iron ore margin is expected to stay slightly negative in the near term.

items.title: India’s steel expansion sharpens focus on raw material security
points: The draft National Steel Policy Vision 2047 targets crude steel capacity of 604 million metric tons/year by 2047, up from 220 million mt/year in fiscal year 2025-26 (April-March), while crude steel production is projected to reach 531 million mt from 170…
The government is prioritizing greater use of domestic resources to support that growth, Minister of State for Heavy Industries and Steel Bhupathiraju Srinivasa Varma said.

“To reach our target of 300 million tons and beyond, our focus must remain sharp on three core areas: beneficiation of low-grade iron ore, building a stronger domestic coking coal base, and securing critical minerals,” Varma said.

Iron ore demand is projected to rise to 772 million mt by 2047 from 299 million mt in 2025, while coking coal requirement is forecast at 236 million mt, up from 72 million mt, according to the draft policy.
India imports about 92% of its coking coal requirement.

items.title: Goldman Sachs: Oil Is Estimated to Ease in 2027 as Suppliers Adapt to Hormuz Disruption
points: Oil is forecast to ease gradually in 2027 as suppliers in the Middle East adapt to disruption from the war in Iran, according to Goldman Sachs Research.

Our commodities analysts expect benchmark Brent crude to average $88 per barrel in 2027 under their base case assumption of no definitive diplomatic breakthrough in Iran and no re-escalation with major long-term damage to oil infrastructure.

Under the same base case scenario, they project that Brent will fall from $93 per barrel today (as of November 17) to $78 by early December 2027 as a sizable surplus decreases Brent’s fair value from $90 per barrel today to the high $70s by the end of 2027.

The key driver was a rise in the supply of oil from the Persian Gulf in October—Goldman Sachs Research estimates that Persian Gulf crude exports recovered in October to their 2025 average, increasing 2 million barrels per day compared with the previous month.

items.title: Temporary toll plaza at Arikkady dismantled
points: The temporary toll plaza at Arikkady on National Highway 66, which had triggered a major political controversy and public protests in Kasaragod district ahead of the Assembly election, was finally dismantled.
Workers of the Uralungal Labour Contract Cooperative Society (ULCCS) began dismantling the temporary structure using a crane on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
They said the entire structure, including the toll booths, would be removed from the site soon.
The controversy erupted after toll collection began at Arikkady following the completion by the ULCCS of the 39-km stretch of National Highway 66 between Talapady and Chengala.
The toll collection triggered widespread protests among residents.
Subsequently, The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) suspended toll collection at the Arikkany plaza on February 3, 2026.
However, the temporary structure remained at the site even after toll collection was suspended.
